narrative:
The model predicted a 72.7% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability is well above the acceptance threshold, your law school application was rejected.

The decision was driven primarily by three factors from your academic record. Your class ranking at the end of your third year was the strongest influence and pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. You placed in the second decile, noticeably lower than the average of roughly sixth-decile performance among students who were accepted. Your first-year ranking was the second most important factor and also worked against you; you finished in the third decile compared with an average around the sixth decile for admitted students. These two early indicators of how you performed relative to your classmates outweighed everything else in the model’s eyes.

Your undergraduate GPA of 3.50 was the third most influential piece of information, but it worked in the opposite direction. This score is higher than the 3.23 average among accepted students and therefore pulled the prediction slightly toward success. Unfortunately, the positive effect of your strong GPA was not large enough to overcome the impact of your lower class rankings.

You should focus on strengthening your academic record and consider retaking the LSAT or enrolling in a structured bar-preparation course before reapplying. Improving your class standing in future semesters and raising your LSAT score would directly address the factors that most hurt your current application.
